source.title: Simplicity bias and optimization threshold in two-layer ReLU networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present. No apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies whether overparameterized networks can fail to interpolate noisy training data yet generalize well, using a two-layer ReLU regression setup and train/test loss measurements. This is a conceptual test of the claim’s generalization behavior, but it does not test the claim’s random-label memorization comparison or most mapped conditions.
record.gate_note: The paper tests an optimization threshold as training-set size grows and reports train loss, test loss, and neuron alignment. It does not test fitting random labels. Its results use a noisy regression task and do not directly establish the claim’s natural-label classification setting. Figure-only loss curves are described qualitatively in the text; exact plotted values are not recoverable. Cited results from other works are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures sample-size-dependent interpolation and generalization in noisy synthetic regression. None of V1–V8 names this comparison. It does not compare random with natural labels, sweep width, or test the other specified interventions or measures. Its Adam–SGD comparison is outside V4's image and language benchmarks. Appendix B explicitly distinguishes its phenomenon from double descent.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. Under restrictive linear-regression assumptions, the authors prove that small-initialization gradient flow converges to a non-interpolating estimator built from OLS fits on two data subsets, despite overparameterization. Experiments beyond those assumptions show approximately OLS-like predictions and near-noise-floor test loss at sufficiently large sample sizes. Early alignment explains the theoretical result; whether that mechanism explains similar behavior in complex models remains unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: Two-layer ReLU regression network trained on noisy linear data; SGD experiments and a gradient-flow analysis. The paper tests an optimization-threshold phenomenon rather than random-label memorization or the claim versions’ classification comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome changes with training-set size and dimension; the threshold is around n⋆ = 3000 at d = 5, interpolation stops around n = 10 000 at d = 10, and OLS-like behavior begins around n = 80 000 at d = 10. For a 5-ReLU teacher, interpolation stops around n = 2000 but losses close to the noise level occur around n⋆ = 17 000. Appendix experiments report similar behavior with GeLU and Adam.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed width, increasing sample size can change noisy regression training from interpolation with elevated test loss to non-interpolation with test loss near the noise floor. Related behavior occurs with GeLU, Adam, higher dimension and a five-ReLU teacher.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small-initialization two-layer networks can generalize well through non-interpolating solutions beyond a sample-size-dependent optimization threshold in noisy regression.

fits_no_version.finding: The fraction of neurons strongly aligned with OLS increases between the tested sample sizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this regression setup, larger training sets produce stronger directional concentration of neurons around OLS.

fits_no_version.finding: Continued training with a decaying learning rate changes loss only slightly and does not restore interpolation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The attained non-interpolating solution persists under the tested SGD continuation schedule.

record.problems: The theorem relies on a specific linear data model, restrictive distribution and initialization assumptions, and a large sample threshold n ≳ d³ log d. Experiments use a toy problem with fixed dimensions and a single stated network width. Several comparisons are qualitative descriptions of figures rather than exact numerical values. The paper notes that the experimental setting differs from the theorem assumptions and that a few misaligned neurons make training loss slightly smaller and test loss slightly larger than OLS.
record.rows_left_out: No more than 60 rows were needed. Figure-only exact loss values are not reconstructed; qualitative results described in the text are recorded in the corresponding rows.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe, including chance held-out performance with random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD generalization on image-classification or language benchmarks under the specified tuning regimes and remedies.
Batch-size penalties under fixed epoch budgets and changes to training recipes that recover performance.
Dropout's effects on held-out error and its interactions with dataset size, augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap correlations and ranking against alternative measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized versus randomly selected examples.

record.verdict_notes: No verdicts are warranted for V1–V8. Failure to interpolate in this regression setting does not contradict V1's demonstrated classification results, and fixed-width sample-size sweeps do not test V2. Qualitative textual results remain usable even when exact plotted losses are unavailable.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels for the specified architectures and training recipes.
Width sweep beyond interpolation threshold and test error as a function of width.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier comparison and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizer comparison on image-classification or language benchmarks.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations to large-batch recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error and interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness or comparison of generalization measures.
Removal and retraining of memorized examples and the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.operation_detail: Varied training-set size n and measured train loss at convergence.

conditions.value: linear model with Gaussian inputs and centered Gaussian noise, variance σ² = 0.09

rows.measure: Training loss at convergence as a function of training-set size.
rows.value: For smaller training sets, the final estimator interpolates the data at convergence; beyond an optimization threshold around n⋆ = 3000, it does not interpolate and the training loss is only slightly smaller than the OLS training loss.
rows.note: Qualitative statements from the text describe the plotted curve; no exact loss values are stated for individual n values.
rows.check: The interpolation result is reported correctly but cannot establish any listed version. Initialization is internally inconsistent in the source: Section 5 gives variance 10^-5/m, whereas Appendix A.1 renders it as 10^-5/sqrt(m); flag this discrepancy.
